pages.title: OpenWheel
pages.subtitle: Build guide · DIY release 1 · 4 × 2" filters
pages.note: Parts: docs/BOM.md (P = printed, M = CNC plate, B = bought, E = electronics). Before you start: print the parts, order the plates and the PCB, and buy the hardware. Tools: hex keys 1.5 / 2 mm, micrometer or caliper, fine sandpaper on a flat plate, vice, soldering iron, USB-C cable.

pages.title: Standoffs
pages.note: File or sand both ends square until all 12 standoffs have the same length (micrometer). They set the 21 mm stack: unequal standoffs bend the plates and tilt the filters.

checks.text: All 12 within 0.02 mm
Lengths differ

pages.title: Hall sensor and firmware
pages.note: Solder the A3144 into the J4 pads from the back of the board (the side without parts): branded face (the narrow face with the bevelled edges and the marking) toward the wheel centre, so pin 1 (VCC) is on pad 1. Leads straight; the far end of the sensor 17 mm from the board. Then flash the firmware: hold CCW while plugging in USB (DFU), see the README.

checks.text: Branded face toward the wheel centre, 17 mm from the board
Sensor turned round: pins 1 and 3 swapped

pages.title: Magnets
pages.note: Board on USB, ASCOM setup dialog → Magnet polarity: hold each magnet to the sensor and mark the side that switches it. That side goes outward. Press the 10 magnets into the rim pockets in groups of 4, 3, 2 and 1, all the same way round, and glue them (CA glue). Let it cure.

checks.text: All marked sides face outward
One magnet reversed: that slot is never found

pages.title: Shaft
pages.note: Press the shaft into the wheel bore with a vice or an arbor press, straight, never with a hammer. The crush ribs in the bore hold it. The disc side of the wheel later faces the camera plate.

checks.text: Wheel runs true when spun
Wheel wobbles

pages.title: Camera plate bearing
pages.note: From the inner side (no counterbores): shim, then the bearing with its flange on the shim. Glue the bearing if it sits loose (retaining compound).

checks.text: Bearing just below the outer face
Bearing sticks out of the outer face

pages.title: Front plate bearing
pages.note: Same as step 5, on the inner side of the front plate (the side without counterbores, shown from below).

checks.text: Bearing just below the outer face
Bearing sticks out of the outer face

pages.title: Standoffs on the camera plate
pages.note: 8 screws from the outer face into the 8 ring standoffs. The 4 standoffs at the motor box are only placed now: the front screws (step 17) and the motor-box screws (step 14) hold them.

checks.text: Standoffs upright, screws flush in the counterbores
Screw head above the plate face

pages.title: Shell
pages.note: Lower the shell over the standoffs until the plate sits in its recess. If the plate doesn't drop in without a gap, reprint the shell scaled 100.1–100.4 % in X/Y (Z 100 %).

checks.text: Plate sits in the recess, no gap
Gap or tilted plate: light leak

pages.title: Wheel (dry fit)
pages.note: Shim, wheel with its disc side down (toward the camera plate), shim. First without filters: the next step fits the hub height.

checks.text: Wheel sits centred on the bearing
Shim missing

pages.title: Dry fit: hub height
pages.note: Screw the front plate on. The wheel must turn freely with no axial play. If it binds, take the plate off and sand the end of the hub flat on fine paper (12 mm → about 11.8 mm). Then take the front plate and the wheel out again.

checks.text: Turns freely, no play
Binds (sand) or rattles (too much sanded)

pages.title: Filters
pages.note: Drop each filter into its seat. Three screws per filter, an O-ring under each head. Tighten gently: the screws cut their own thread in the plastic. Note which filter is in which numbered slot; the names are set later in the driver.

checks.text: Filter can't rattle
Screw stripped: overtightened

pages.title: Friction roller
pages.note: Push a piece of 2×4 mm silicone tube over the Ø3 motor shaft and cut it flush with the shaft end. It is the roller that drives the wheel rim (not shown in the drawings).

checks.text: Tube tight, can't turn on the shaft
Tube longer than the shaft

pages.title: Motor into the box
pages.note: Motor into the box with its flange toward the plate side (shown from below). The two ear screws go in from inside the box through the slots. Leave them loose.

checks.text: Motor slides in its slots
Screw longer than 10 mm: it reaches the wheel

pages.title: Motor box on
pages.note: Turn the stack over. Screw the box to the 4 motor-box standoffs from inside the box. The motor shaft with its roller now stands in the chamber next to the wheel position.

checks.text: Box flat on the camera plate
Roller hits the shell

pages.title: Wheel in
pages.note: Turn the stack back. Shim, wheel with filters, shim, as in step 9.

checks.text: Wheel sits on the bearing, turns by hand
Shim missing

pages.title: Set the motor
pages.note: Turn the stack over again. Push the motor in its slots toward the wheel until the roller presses on the wheel rim, and hold it there while you tighten the two ear screws from inside the box. Firm enough not to slip, light enough that the wheel still turns by hand.

checks.text: Wheel turns by hand, roller rolls with it
Roller slips, or the wheel jams

pages.title: Front plate
pages.note: Tighten the screws crosswise. Filters are changed later the same way: front plate off, 12 screws (reachable with an OAG or adapter mounted).

checks.text: Wheel turns freely by hand
Wheel touches a standoff

pages.title: Motor wires and PCB
pages.note: Solder the 4 motor wires to the J3 pads on the component side; cut the pins flush on the back (the board sits 0.3 mm above the motor). Lower the board onto the 3 bosses, components toward the lid, guiding the Hall sensor through the box and the plate slot. 3 screws. The sensor reaches about 4 mm into the chamber, next to the wheel rim.

checks.text: Sensor passes the slot straight
Sensor bent or pinched

pages.title: Lid
pages.note: Clip the lid on: + (CW) and − (CCW) pads over the buttons, USB-C opening over the socket.

checks.text: Both pads click and spring back
A pad stays pressed

pages.title: Done: power up and calibrate
pages.note: Plug in USB-C. Calibrate once: long press CW (or hold CW while plugging in). The wheel turns, finds the magnets and stores 4 slots. Then install the ASCOM or INDI driver and name the filters (user manual).

checks.text: Calibration finds 4 slots
Both LEDs blink: error, see the user manual
